results.title: Consumer Sentiment Was Weaker in August, per Michigan Survey

results.content:
## Key Takeaways

The University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index final reading fell to 51.7 in August, a 6.3% decrease from July.

Joanne Hsu, the director of surveys, made the following comments: [...] Consumer sentiment falls in August after two previous months of improvement. The final August reading for the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index came in at 51.7. This marks a 6.3% (3.5 points) decrease from July and below the preliminary reading of 51.0. Consumer sentiment sits 11.2% below where it was a year ago and is currently below the 1st percentile in the series' history.

results.title: Consumer Sentiment Falls in August - dshort

results.content:
The University of Michigan updated its consumer sentiment index Friday with a preliminary August reading of 51, down about 8% from the final July index reading of 55.2.

The final August consumer sentiment index will be released on the 28th.

The school’s consumer sentiment tracker goes back decades and hit an all-time low in May. It had shown improvement across June and July before the downturn this month.
